title: Warming richness contrasts had intervals across zero in four Cedar Creek samples in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether a reported warming richness deficit in 16-species grassland plantings also appeared in separate four-species plantings. We used 432 complete harvest records from nine whole plots per group at Cedar Creek in 2017-2022. Four paired tests covered two planting groups and two time periods. Heated-minus-control contrasts were -0.019 recorded species in each period in four-species plots, and -0.796 and -0.574 in 16-species plots. All four corrected plot intervals included zero. Direct planting-group differences were also uncertain. Single-plot omissions kept the full-period 16-species estimate negative. Under a simple multiplicative detection model, about 9% lower heated detection could erase that pooled descriptive deficit. This is a conditional threshold, not an estimated error rate. Moving harvest strips, few plots, planted composition, shared weather and one site limit inference. The periods reuse plots and do not provide independent regional replication. No pollution effect or local extinction is established. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, exact input hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Paired heated-minus-control richness estimates. The left panel gives four primary estimates with 98.75% plot t intervals. The right panel gives annual descriptive means. Groups use different plots at the same site. Periods share plots.
